ifuto-replay.config.title: Ifuto Replay Settings
ifuto-replay.config.hint: Controls are the buttons in the top-left of the pause menu (ESC). Packets are stored as-is, so recording stays light (playback preview and video export are supported)
ifuto-replay.menu.marker.tooltip: Drop a marker at the current time (only while recording).
ifuto-replay.list.title: Recordings
ifuto-replay.list.hint: Saved recordings (only headers are read, never the packet bodies)
ifuto-replay.list.delete.tooltip: Delete this file. Press again to confirm.
ifuto-replay.list.play.tooltip: Feeds the stored packets into a vanilla world and plays them back (this disconnects you from the current world)
ifuto-replay.list.play_confirm_message: Playback disconnects you from the current world/server. Continue?
ifuto-replay.config.auto_record.tooltip: Start recording as soon as you join a world or server.
ifuto-replay.config.record_client_packet: Also store the packets you send to the server (movement, clicks, chat). Turning it off makes the file even smaller.
ifuto-replay.config.compression.tooltip: Compression applied while writing, on the writer thread, so the game is barely affected. Packets are compressed in 16 KB blocks. Strong: recommended (measured at about 21-24% of the raw size). Max: a little smaller still, but uses about twice the CPU
ifuto-replay.config.skip_keep_alive.tool: Leave out keep-alive and ping packets, which only keep the connection alive.
ifuto-replay.config.save_registries.tool: Keeps a copy of the dynamic registries (biomes, dimensions, ...) at the start of the file, so a replay can be played back later even from a different world.
ifuto-replay.config.mask_address.tooltip: Shows the server address as ******** in preview and export (remembered once enabled).
ifuto-replay.config.max_file_size.toolti: Stop and save automatically once the file grows past this. 0 means unlimited.
ifuto-replay.config.max_duration.tooltip: Stop and save automatically after this much time. 0 means unlimited.
ifuto-replay.config.show_indicator.toolt: While recording, show the elapsed time and file size in a screen corner (stop from the pause menu).
ifuto-replay.config.indicator_position.t: Which corner the recording HUD sits in.
ifuto-replay.config.notify_chat.tooltip: Print recording start, save and marker messages to the chat.
ifuto-replay.message.not_in_game: §7[Replay]§r Join a world before starting a recording
ifuto-replay.message.io_error: §7[Replay]§r Could not open the save folder (check the save folder setting)
ifuto-replay.message.partial_start: §7[Replay]§r Recording started mid-session, so this file cannot be played back (rejoin the server or turn on "Auto record")
ifuto-replay.preview.title: Replay
ifuto-replay.preview.shaders_missing: Only available when Iris Shaders is installed
ifuto-replay.preview.error_no_join: This recording starts mid-session, so the world cannot be rebuilt. Rejoin the server before recording, or turn on "Auto record".
ifuto-replay.list.export.tooltip: Render the recording to a video file (FPS and resolution are chosen afterwards)
ifuto-replay.export.title: Export video
ifuto-replay.export.hint: Exporting %s. FPS and resolution are independent of the recording, so you can redo them any time.
ifuto-replay.export.fps.tooltip: Frames per second of the video. Unrelated to the recorded fps (higher = smoother and slower)
ifuto-replay.export.resolution.tooltip: Independent of the window size (odd values are rounded down to even)
ifuto-replay.export.start.tooltip: Timestamp to start the export at
ifuto-replay.export.end.tooltip: Timestamp to end the export at
ifuto-replay.export.ffmpeg.tooltip: The ffmpeg executable. "ffmpeg" works if it is on your PATH.
ifuto-replay.export.name: File name
ifuto-replay.export.error_message:
%s

Check that ffmpeg is installed and that the path is correct.
ifuto-replay.export.bitrate.tooltip: Higher is nicer and bigger (10000-20000 is a good range for 1080p60)
ifuto-replay.export.error_stalled: No progress for a while, so the export was stopped. Try a lower resolution or another recording.
ifuto-replay.config.snapshot_radius.tool: When you start recording mid-session, save the terrain and entities within this radius. 0 = don't save (mid-session recordings won't be playable)
ifuto-replay.message.snapshot: Recording started mid-session, so the current world state was saved along with it
ifuto-replay.message.disk_low: Only %s MB left where recordings are saved. Recording stops automatically when it runs out
ifuto-replay.message.disk_critical: Less than %s MB left, so the recording was saved and stopped
ifuto-replay.message.size_warning: Getting close to the file size limit (%s / %s MB)
ifuto-replay.config.flush_interval.toolt: How often buffered data is moved to the file. Shorter = less memory, longer = fewer disk writes
ifuto-replay.config.low_disk_space.toolt: Warn when the free space drops below this (0 = never watch)
Save and stop recording when the free space drops below this (0 = never stop)
ifuto-replay.config.memory.tooltip: How much may sit in memory waiting to be written. 0 = decide from the environment (recommended)
ifuto-replay.config.audio_mode.tooltip: Audio is captured while you record and written to a separate file. If it can't be captured, recording continues without audio
ifuto-replay.config.audio_device.tooltip: Windows: device name such as Stereo Mix / Linux: pactl name (.monitor) / macOS: a virtual device such as BlackHole
Find an audio device and fill it in (found devices are listed in the tooltip)
ifuto-replay.message.audio_failed: Could not record audio (%s). Recording continues
ifuto-replay.export.include_audio.toolti: Mux the audio that was captured alongside the recording into the video
ifuto-replay.export.include_vc.tooltip: Include Simple Voice Chat voices (captured as a separate voice-only track)
ifuto-replay.export.include_vc.tooltip_o: This recording has no Minecraft-only audio, so excluding voice chat drops the audio track entirely
ifuto-replay.export.audio_dropped: + no audio (there is no voice-chat-free track)
ifuto-replay.config.record_voice_chat.to: Record Simple Voice Chat voices into a separate file (include or drop them when exporting)
ifuto-replay.message.audio_fallback: Could not capture Minecraft-only audio, recording whole-PC audio instead (%s). Change it under "Record audio" in the settings
ifuto-replay.menu.stop.tooltip: Stop recording and save what you have so far
ifuto-replay.menu.clip.tooltip: Save the last few seconds as a recording. Only available in clip mode.
ifuto-replay.config.clip_mode.tooltip: Record continuously like Medal, then save backwards from the moment you press "Save clip". Nothing is kept unless you press it.
ifuto-replay.config.clip_seconds.tooltip: How far back to save (15 s up to 4 h). The result can be slightly longer because of how clips are split
ifuto-replay.message.clip_started: Recording in clip mode, keeping the last %s
ifuto-replay.message.clip_empty: Not enough recorded yet for a clip
ifuto-replay.message.clip_stopped: Clip mode stopped (anything you did not save is gone)
ifuto-replay.message.clip_disabled: Clip mode is off — you can turn it on in the settings
ifuto-replay.config.clip_keep.tooltip: Saved clips older than this are deleted automatically, together with their audio. Choose "Forever" to keep them until you delete them yourself
ifuto-replay.config.clip_buffer.tooltip: Upper limit for the temporary files. Auto keeps just what the measured write speed needs and drops the oldest segments past that, which also keeps the amount written to your SSD down
ifuto-replay.message.clip_no_space: Not enough free space to save the clip (%s needed)
ifuto-replay.export.realtime.tooltip: On: every frame is drawn at the same pace as the original, so effects that look at real time (motion blur accumulation, temporal shaders, effects that fade with time) behave exactly as they did live. It takes as long as the recording. Off: frames are drawn as fast as the GPU allows (much faster, but those effects change)
ifuto-replay.config.record_particles.too: Records the particles the client spawns itself: block breaking debris, footsteps, mod effects. Ones sent by the server are already in the packet stream, so they are not recorded twice
